%n [...] urruqu? zīma
#note: The tentative reading @i{urruqu}, i.e. “very yellow/pale” needs collation. However, it is, to my mind, the only reading to fit the context, as @i{warāqu} - both in G and D stem - is well-attested to designate a frightened face turning pale, see @bib{RN2721@A2 231f. s.v. arāqu}. A translation to this effect is also suggested by @bib{RN262@98f.}, who, however, leaves the signs in question uninterpreted. Other proposed readings are difficult to maintain: @akk{tu#-ru-qu}, suggested to be derived from @i{turruku} “darkened” (thus @bib{RN262@304f.}, @bib{AdalıDiss@250 with fn. 124}) is problematic for the difference in its third radical; Understanding @akk{ru-qu} as @i{ruqqu} “thin part” (a part of the exta, thus @bib{LongmanDiss@286}) is equally improbable, as this word hardly occurs without a defining @i{nomen rectum}, see @bib{RN2721@R 418f. ad 3}.

#note: @bib{RN2365@163 ad l. 21} suggests a restoration @akk{[e] tul-ta-[bil têrta] li-par-qud pa-gar-ka}. @bib{RN262@304f., 336} reads @akk{KI#.TA#} for @i{erṣetu} “earth”. The logogram, however, if read thus, should represent a derivative of @i{šaplu} “low”. She also has @i{lipparqud} “may it lie”. As she points out herself (@bib{RN262@305 ad 21}, one would expect @i{lipparqid}. Other possibilities would be to read @akk{UD TAR} as @i{tamhaṣ} “you hit” or @i{uttar} “I/he increase(s) (sth.)”. A reading @i{tamšīl} “likeness” in the construct state (thus @bib{LongmanDiss@286}) can be excluded on the basis of the apparent nominative/accusative form @i{pagarka} “your body”.

#note: For the tentative restoration @i{šalamtaš īmi} “he became like a corpse”, see @bib{schaudig_explaining_2019@386}. @bib{RN262@304f.} proposes to restore the end of the line as @akk{GAR-[un]}, i.e. @i{iškun} “he placed, i.e. issued”. The preserved traces in NinNA4 in ll. 115-117 fit @akk{šu₂-nu} better than the reading @akk{ši}, proposed in most earlier editions of this composition. %n balu bīri šīri tāka[lti] ul ubba[l qātī?]
#note: This reading essentially follows @bib{RN164@353}, who translates “Without divination (of liver), flesh, and entr[ails], [I should not] lay [hand on them to kill?]”. The reading @akk{ba-lu bi-ri še-ri ta-ka[l!-ti ...]}, he states (@bib{RN164@356}), was communicated to him by von Soden. The same reading for the first half of the line was suggested by Sommerfeld (@i{apud} @bib{RN262@322, fn. 125}), who, however, restores @i{pānī} instead of @i{qātī} (“werde ich keine Nachsicht üben”). As @bib{RN262@322, fn. 125} points out, his interpretation would lack the expected change in attitude on the part of Narām-Sîn. She reads (@bib{RN262@322}) @i{balu bīri šērēta u}[@i{mmudu}?] @i{ul ubba}[@i{l qātī}?] “Without omens, I will not bring myself to [impose] punishments.”; similarly @bib{RN262@104f.}: @akk{ba-lu bi-ri še-re-ta u₂?# [...] ul ub-b[al? ...]} “Without an inspection (of the entrails) I will not @i{ap}[@i{ply}] @i{a punishment}.”. There are, however, two problems with Goodnick Westenholz’s interpretation: Firstly, it should be @i{qātī}-SUF @i{wabālu ana ...}, and secondly, the supposed plural form of @i{šērtu} “punishment” should be @i{šērēti}.
